comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: SETUP AND CONSTRAINTS. Standalone study at /Users/joeoakhart/plan-review-bakeoff, its own git repo (~60 commits), deliberately independent of the rebar ticket system. Compares 4 plan-review sources on identical plans. NO new rebar plan reviews were run at any point: rebar's arm is extracted from existing signed REVIEW_RESULT sidecars. Arms are the real tools, not distilled prompts: rebar sidecars; Compound Engineering ce-doc-review 3.24.0 (persona fan-out, real subagents); superpowers 6.3.0 writing-plans + plan-document-reviewer-prompt; mini-swe-agent 2.4.6 real CLI in an isolated venv on anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6. Skills load via ~/.claude/skills/ symlinks because plugin-path skills do not resolve on this box. Work is organised into three waves, defined in WAVES.md.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: WAVE 1 - METHOD. 10 rebar tickets, each contributing a BLOCK-state plan and its later PASS-state plan, giving a within-ticket control. Ticket state is reconstructed with 'git archive <tickets_sha> <dir> | tar -x' into a PLAIN directory - never a git worktree, because REBAR_TRACKER_DIR on a worktree makes rebar run store maintenance and delete history. Six metrics per METHODOLOGY.md: TP requires accurate AND material; an FP requires opening the cited file at the pinned SHA and quoting the disproving excerpt (never asserted from reasoning); nits are accurate-but-immaterial; UNVERIFIABLE is its own bucket. Judging is delegated to independent subagents under a binding contract in harness/JUDGE_INSTRUCTIONS.md; the orchestrator does not score.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: WAVE 1 - RESULTS at 16 scored runs. Rows/TP/FP/nits/precision/materiality: rebar 269/108/11/84/91%/53%; Compound Eng 257/202/2/56/99%/78%; superpowers 118/84/4/33/95%/69%; mini-swe-agent 77/48/1/26/98%/64%. Severity honesty (share of an arm's own nits it marked blocking): superpowers 3%, rebar 6%, mini 15%, CE 27%. Metric 5, TPs only rebar found: 61 across 23 criteria (E6 10, T8 7, T9 7, E1 6, G6 6). Metric 6, TPs rebar missed: 201, of which only 2 are genuine gaps (no criterion covers them) - every other one is a MISS, where a criterion exists and did not fire. E4 and G6 repeatedly stay silent on plans squarely in their remit.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: WAVE 1 - CONFOUNDS, all recorded rather than corrected. (1) PRIOR-REVIEW EXPOSURE, the largest: every plan was authored against rebar's own criteria and pre-hardened by earlier rebar reviews (median 4, max 15), so rebar is scored on finding defects in plans it already cleaned while the other 3 arms read them blind. 2127-348c-PASS at 8 prior reviews yields rebar 0 TP. On 2948-48e5-BLOCK, the ONLY run with prior_reviews=0, rebar scored 10 TP / 0 FP - perfect precision on the single fair read in the study. (2) DET-ONLY runs: 17 of 220 candidates have metrics.llm_calls==0, rebar blocking at its deterministic precheck without any content review; all are BLOCK, reported separately and never pooled. (3) INDETERMINATE is PASS-only: 181 findings, 20% of rebar's PASS output, 0 on any BLOCK run; never scored FP per METHODOLOGY but surfaced as contradicted_unrated (7). (4) mini's step budget is not uniform (150 steps for most runs, 260 for one).

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: WAVE 1 - CORRECTIONS MADE DURING THE STUDY. INPUT ASYMMETRY was the largest and changed results materially: rebar reads child and referenced tickets, while the other arms initially got the parent description alone. On the 86ac epic, 5 of rebar's 6 unique TPs were child-ticket contradictions the others could not see. 14 runs were superseded to superseded/parent-only/ and re-run with related material; CE went 21->20 findings but 0->6 P0, superpowers 6->9 findings and 3->5 blocking. DUP RATE was never a duplication rate: it netted merges against SPLITS (a judge splitting one row into 2 issues pushes distinct above emitted), so it went negative. Replaced by a signed 'net merged - split' count: rebar +49, CE -3, sp -3, mini +2. rebar's +49 is the real duplication signal. PROVENANCE: 2 CE outputs no longer matched the judged snapshot; 1 recovered by verbatim title match and frozen at runs/judged/, 1 genuinely lost (a 4th concurrent CE execution alive on disk for 6 minutes) and now carrying a caveat naming all 13 rows. A sweep of all 72 arm-cells found no third case, and harness/judged.py now snapshots arm outputs at judging time and refuses clobbering.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: WAVE 1 - REBAR FAILURE MODES OBSERVED, all from judge adjudications. (1) RECALL, NOT PRECISION, is the weakness: 201 missed TPs against 61 unique, and only 2 of the 201 are genuine gaps. The rest are misses where a criterion exists and stays silent. (2) ROUTING: on 62d9-9f6d-BLOCK rebar's A1 finding enumerated the correct evidence AND prescribed exactly the fix CE and mini prescribed, then filed it at severity:none, priority:0.0. It had the answer and scored it at zero. (3) SELF-CORROBORATION inflating a false positive: on bda8-370d-BLOCK rebar claimed add_issues_to_epic raises NotImplementedError before any HTTP call; in jira 3.10.5 the method POSTs with no guard and that string appears nowhere in the package. rebar then cited its OWN plan-review cache as corroborating evidence, turning 1 error into 3 rows, 2 of them blocking. The disproof was already on the ticket it was reviewing. (4) DUPLICATION: +49 net merged rows, the only arm that emits one issue under several criteria; on 62d9-9f6d-BLOCK 11 rows were 8 distinct issues, overstating by 38%. (5) DETECTED-THEN-WITHDRAWN: on bda8-370d-BLOCK 3 of 13 missed issues were found and then suppressed below threshold.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: WAVE 1 - ARM CHARACTERISATION. Compound Engineering is the best FINDER: highest recall (202 TP), highest precision (99%) and materiality (78%), but the worst severity honesty (27% of its own nits marked blocking, including P3 wording fixes) and ZERO BLOCK/PASS discrimination (101 TP on each). superpowers is the best SIGNAL-TO-NOISE: 84 TP from 118 rows, nearly CE's hit rate on under half the volume, and the best severity honesty of any arm at 3%. mini-swe-agent is smallest (77 rows, 98% precision) with zero BLOCK/PASS discrimination, but found 1 of the study's only 2 genuine gaps by going OUTSIDE the plan's stated tree to check a claim against the real tickets branch - no other arm did that. It is also the only arm with a hard dollar cost (.38 avg, .28 worst) and a catastrophic failure mode: at an insufficient step budget it burns the full budget and submits nothing (.75 for zero output before a 260-step retry succeeded). STRUCTURAL FACT: of the 201 issues rebar missed, 156 were found by exactly ONE arm and only 11 by three. The reviewers are near-disjoint - they look at different things rather than being better and worse versions of one instrument. That is the strongest argument in the data for an ensemble.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: WAVE 1 - VERDICT. rebar is NOT categorically worse. It contributes 61 TPs no other arm found across 23 criteria; it has the second-best severity honesty (6% vs CE's 27%), which matters disproportionately for something that gates; it was the only arm to examine security at all (a live PAT-in-logs path on bda8, judged understated rather than overstated); and it is the only arm that is a GATE rather than a document - a signed attestation pinned to a code SHA and material fingerprint that blocks the claim. Its raw numbers are also depressed by the prior-review confound described above. The honest summary: CE for recall, superpowers for signal-to-noise, mini for out-of-tree factual grounding, rebar for gating. The configuration the data supports is running both rebar (gating) and a finder (advisory), not choosing one.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: WAVE 2 - THE FLOOR MECHANISM, read from source. rising_floor_drop at src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/decide.py:105-119 drops iff novelty>=0.7 and priority<0.4, applied by _apply_floor_to_verdict in llm/plan_review/floors.py:24-57, gated by _maybe_apply_rising_floor in llm/plan_review/__init__.py:114-165. IT SUPPRESSES THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT WAS ASSUMED: it drops NOVEL LOW-PRIORITY findings, the noise an edit stirs up. A prior-round blocking finding is a carryover with novelty~0 and is EXPLICITLY KEPT - there is no 'already-seen gets suppressed' behaviour, and the predicate exists precisely to protect that case. So 'rebar re-litigates its own remediated findings' was a wrong framing on my part and is retracted. Jurisdiction is ONE bucket: floors.py:36 reads verdict['advisory']; blocking, indeterminate and overflow are never iterated. That explains 2948-48e5-PASS, where all 5 preconditions held, the floor path RAN, and it floored nothing because 25 of 27 findings were indeterminate. Preconditions (remediation_mode.py:33, all must hold): plan fingerprint CHANGED, verified_at_sha UNCHANGED, regver unchanged, prior sidecar present, within 60 minutes. Signed prior NOT required. No config flag - the off switch was retired in story 4cdf, so it is on by default.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: WAVE 2 Q2 - CONVERGENCE, corrected. A MEASUREMENT DEFECT was found and fixed mid-analysis: floored findings retain decision=='advisory', not 'dropped' - of 1,191 findings with a non-null drop_reason, ZERO carry decision=='dropped'. The first pass tested only decision=='dropped' and so counted every floor drop as shown to the author. Corrected test is decision=='dropped' OR drop_reason is not None. Corrected results on 399 tickets with >=3 reviews (2,711 plan reviews across 778 tickets): THE TWO AXES DISAGREE. Verdict converges - blocking findings 2.04->1.50->1.15, 41.6% of tickets monotone, 96.2% end at zero blocking. Author-visible text does NOT - 7.54, 7.30, 6.96, 7.21, 7.74, 7.69, 8.59, 8.20, 7.23, 8.21 across rounds 1-10, a shallow dip then a rise past the start; 20.3% monotone, 5.8% end at zero. The driver is NOVELTY, not resurrection: 69.6% of what an author sees in round N was never shown before, and on BYTE-IDENTICAL material (unchanged fingerprint) it is still 57.1% - a nondeterminism floor. Resurrection is 0.4% and block->floored is 0.0% in every segment. The floor fires on 20.4% of rounds and removes 6.6% of findings overall, 15.6% on eligible transitions vs 0.8% on ineligible. drop_reason breakdown: 1,088 novelty, 23 completion, 20 drift, 0 duplicate - so the floor is NOT what would address the +49 duplication problem. Era segmentation is moot: 99.5% of reviews postdate the 2026-07-15 BLOCK-loop fix.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: WAVE 3 - SOURCING (in progress, no reviews dispatched). 20 plans to be sourced from OUTSIDE rebar, because Wave 1 measures 4 reviewers on ONE Python codebase in ONE house style written by authors who had the reviewer's own criteria in front of them - every Wave 1 number is entangled with that. Rules: epics only (BUGS EXCLUDED - a bug report is not a plan), substantial (4,000+ chars of plan content; Wave 1 runs 11,000-85,000), publicly readable, deliberate non-Python language spread (Java, Ruby, NextJS/TypeScript required), and heavy UI emphasis because rebar's corpus is a CLI/library/reconciler with essentially no UI - Compound Engineering's design-lens persona has DECLINED TO ACTIVATE on every Wave 1 run for lack of UI content, so an entire arm of the instrument has never fired. Code grounding IS available for Wave 3: a local checkout is materialized at a PINNED SHA contemporaneous with the issue (not today's HEAD - a plan reviewed against a tree that already implements it scores as nonsense), so all 4 arms read the same code, matching Wave 1's setup. Sourcing runs as 3 disjoint slices: Nava/Jira (navasage.atlassian.net + navapbc org), Java/JVM external OSS (Kafka KIPs, Flink FLIPs, Cassandra CEPs, Kotlin KEEPs), and non-JVM external OSS UI-first (USWDS, GOV.UK, Carbon, Primer, Radix, Rails/Hotwire, framework RFC repos). Best Nava seam identified: OSCER (Ruby, state Medicaid system) and the Strata SDKs (strata-sdk-rails Ruby, strata-sdk-case-management TypeScript, strata-unemployment benefits portal, bao-nguyen-strata-java-sdk). An SDK is an unusually good review target because its plans must reason about a public contract and downstream consumers. Pool is capped at roughly half Nava so the wave does not rebuild the monoculture it exists to break. Internal Jira material carries ticket keys/titles/descriptions/ACs but NOT personal names.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: WAVE 1 CLOSED - FINAL NUMBERS, 20 artifacts / 19 in the comparison (36ab-b649-BLOCK excluded as rebar precheck-only, llm_calls==0, reported separately). Rows/distinct/net-merged/TP/FP/nits/unverifiable: rebar 320/258/+62/123/13/101/21; Compound Eng 306/311/-5/235/3/73/0; superpowers 135/140/-5/97/4/39/0; mini-swe-agent 93/91/+2/60/1/30/0. Precision and materiality: rebar 90%/52% (84% precision if the 11 contradicted-but-unrated indeterminate findings were counted), CE 99%/76%, sp 96%/69%, mini 98%/66%. Severity honesty (own nits marked blocking): sp 3%, rebar 6%, mini 17%, CE 33%. Metric 5, TPs only rebar found: 69. Metric 6, TPs rebar missed: 236 - of which 233 are MISSES (a criterion covers it and did not fire) and only 3 are genuine GAPS. BLOCK/PASS discrimination is weak or absent across the board: rebar 62/61, CE 124/111, sp 54/43, mini 33/27 - no arm cleanly separates a plan rebar blocked from one it passed. Of the 236 issues rebar missed, 183 were found by exactly ONE arm and only 13 by three, so the reviewers remain near-disjoint at full sample.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: WAVE 1 - REPRODUCIBILITY STATE. All 20 runs snapshotted via harness/judged.py: 0 unsnapshotted, 0 count mismatches, 0 drifted, 1 recorded divergence, 1 known-lost. The 1 recorded divergence is 2127-348c-PASS/CE, where the judged 16-row snapshot was recovered by verbatim title match from commit 2946e4b and frozen at runs/judged/; runs/ holds a later 22-row execution preserved as a replicate. The 1 known-lost is eb6e-f43a-PASS/CE: two CE agents were live on that run simultaneously and the judge scored a 13-row synthesis that existed on disk only between commits. Three other CE executions of that arm survive (9, 16 and 19 rows) and none is the judged set; 7 of the 13 judged rows appear nowhere. That artifact now carries a caveat naming all 13 rows. Not re-run and not re-judged, because a fresh run would produce different findings and paper over the gap. Guard added: judged.py snapshots every arm output at judging time with hash and finding-id list, refuses to replace a differing snapshot, and is wired into validate.py; CE_INSTRUCTIONS and SP_INSTRUCTIONS now require a guard check before writing. Side effect worth knowing: .gitignore excluded runs/*.traj.json, so mini trajectories were never in git - the snapshots give that arm its first history protection.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: OPEN THREADS AT PAUSE. Wave 1 is CLOSED at 20 artifacts, RESULTS.md regenerated, working tree committed. NOT YET DONE: Wave 2 Q1 (replicability - a second blank-slate round per plan including a second rebar review, to measure how much each source varies against itself; partial data already exists as accidental replicates in artifacts/judge-replicates/INTER_JUDGE.md and ARM_REPLICATES.md, plus 3 CE replicates on bda8-370d-BLOCK) and Wave 2 Q3 (iterations-to-pass: how many remediate/re-review cycles to pass each non-rebar reviewer, cycle cap 6, grounded in rebar's own history across 747 tickets - mean 2.29, median 2, p75 3, p90 4, p95 6, max 16, 45.6% pass first review). Wave 3 sourcing is in flight across 3 disjoint slices and no Wave 3 reviews have been dispatched. Q2 is complete and corrected. The floor-mechanism read is complete. Design docs: WAVES.md, METHODOLOGY.md, harness/PHASE2_DESIGN.md, harness/JUDGE_INSTRUCTIONS.md, harness/FIDELITY_LOG.md (every deviation, standing ones included: CE cross-model pass skipped on all runs because the codebase is proprietary, nothing applied, mini and superpowers severity vocabularies are harness-imposed, no spec file exists).

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: METHODOLOGICAL FINDING - prior_reviews UNDERCOUNTS, so the study's 'uncontaminated' runs are not. Both judges on the 62d9-9f6d pair found this independently: the BLOCK half records prior_reviews=0 and the PASS half 1, but the ticket's own first comment is headed 'DESCRIPTION SUBSTANTIALLY REWRITTEN (epic e369 plan-review passes 2-8)'. The counter reads low because review-plan fast-fails INDETERMINATE with no LLM spend while a dependency is unclosed, so those hardening rounds were recorded against the EPIC, not the ticket. Consequence: the prior-review confound is WORSE than the manifest reports, and both runs treated as clean reads (2948-48e5-BLOCK and 62d9-9f6d-BLOCK, each at 0) had epic-level hardening the counter does not show. rebar's 10 TP / 0 FP on 2948-48e5-BLOCK should NO LONGER be described as a fully uncontaminated result. Any future measurement of this confound must count epic-level passes, not per-ticket prior_reviews alone. Related, from the same run: rebar's fp:1 understates its inaccuracy roughly 5x in raw claim count - 4 indeterminate findings are refuted by the plan's own text, 3 of them faulting the plan for omitting something it states explicitly (one asks for an AC present verbatim; three ask for a paragraph the plan spends 12 lines on). METHODOLOGY bars these from the FP column because the reviewer withheld a verdict; they are surfaced as contradicted_unrated, 11 corpus-wide.
